# **Forensic Document-Intelligence Architecture for Municipal Weighbridge Evidence Verification: Engineering Robust Extraction under Physical and Optical Degradation**

## **Physical and Optical Degradation Dynamics of Thermal Weighbridge Receipts**

Thermal weighbridge receipts represent an exceptionally hostile document domain for automated optical character recognition and information extraction pipelines1. Unlike commercial laser-printed invoices or born-digital portable document formats, weighbridge documentation is generated at remote municipal civil work sites, aggregate quarries, asphalt plants, and waste transfer stations using compact, direct-thermal point-of-sale printers1. Direct-thermal paper operates through a heat-induced chemical reaction: a base substrate is coated with a solid matrix containing a colorless leuco dye, typically fluoran derivatives, and an acidic organic developer such as bisphenol A or sulfonylureas. When the thermal printhead micro-resistors fire, the heat melts the binder matrix, allowing the dye and developer to fuse, yielding an amorphous, intensely colored state that forms the alphanumeric text.

This chemical bond is inherently unstable over operational lifecycles. Exposure to solar ultraviolet radiation, ambient temperatures exceeding ![][image1], mechanical friction, and plasticizer migration from standard polyvinyl chloride storage jackets induces spontaneous reverse reactions or diffuse background darkening. The visual consequence is contrast collapse: the paper background shifts from bright white to murky gray or mottled brown, while printed glyphs fade toward faint beige or light charcoal3.

Field capture conditions introduce optical and geometric distortions that exacerbate these chemical vulnerabilities2. Mobile telephone captures acquired inside vehicle cabs or scale-house kiosks exhibit steep illumination gradients3. Direct sunlight creates high-specularity whiteouts that bleach pale print, while vehicle chassis or driver hands cast non-linear shadows that cause global binarization algorithms to bifurcate the document into unreadable white and black zones3. Mechanical handling adds non-planar surface curvatures: scale tickets crumpled into pockets exhibit creases and folds that scatter incident light unevenly, break character baselines, and distort inter-word and inter-line spacing2.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| TYPICAL THERMAL WEIGHBRIDGE RECEIPT DEGRADATION PHENOMENOLOGY         |  
\+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+  
|  \[Faded Header\]        METRO WEIGH SCALE \#04                          |  
|  \[Uneven Exposure\]     TICKET: 849201    DATE: 2024-05-12  14:23:09   |  
|  \[Crease / Distortion\] TRUCK ID: H-9921                               |  
|  \[Broken 7-Seg Font\]   GROSS : 38,420 kg  (Broken horizontal bars)    |  
|  \[Oil / Rain Stain\]    TARE  : 14,180 kg  (Local stroke obliteration) |  
|  \[Contrast Collapse\]   NET   : 24,240 kg  (Faint gray on dark gray)   |  
\+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

Thermal printheads frequently suffer from individual resistor failure, known as pin dropouts1. A single blown pin generates a persistent horizontal white void through entire lines of text1. This hardware failure causes fatal character transpositions: an 8 degrades into a 3 or 0, a 6 into a 5, or an E into an F1. Furthermore, environmental contaminants such as liquid asphalt, diesel exhaust, hydraulic fluid, rainwater, and mineral dust produce localized translucent or opaque stains that obliterate character stroke boundaries3. Finally, mobile photographs taken at oblique angles introduce perspective distortion, causing parallel receipt margins to converge and character dimensions to vary non-linearly across the frame2. Standard optical character recognition engines trained on clean, upright document corpuses experience severe performance degradation when processing these degraded artifacts without specialized front-end image restoration1.

## **Image Restoration and Preprocessing Pipeline**

To ensure reliable text detection and character classification, raw visual evidence must traverse a deterministic restoration pipeline that isolates text morphology from thermal and optical noise before routing to downstream recognition models3.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| RESTORATION AND PREPROCESSING PIPELINE STAGES                                                    |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
|  Raw Input Photograph / Scan                                                                     |  
|    |                                                                                             |  
|  \[Stage 1: Document Boundary Detection & Perspective Rectification\]                             |  
|    ├── Grayscale downscale & bilateral filtering (edge preservation)                             |  
|    ├── Morphological gradient \+ Canny edge detection                                             |  
|    └── 4-point contour extraction & Homography perspective warp to canonical flat geometry       |  
|    |                                                                                             |  
|  \[Stage 2: Orientation Correction & Baseline Deskewing\]                                          |  
|    ├── Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) or Radon transform to determine dominant angle θ        |  
|    └── Affine rotation matrix inversion (aligning horizontal text baselines to ±0.5°)           |  
|    |                                                                                             |  
|  \[Stage 3: Illumination Flattening & Contrast Enhancement\]                                       |  
|    ├── Extract Luminance (Y) channel in YUV / LAB color space                                    |  
|    ├── Morphological background estimation (large structural disk kernel)                        |  
|    └── Division normalization: I\_norm \= (I / I\_bg) \* 255 \+ Contrast Limited Adaptive Hist. Eq.   |  
|    |                                                                                             |  
|  \[Stage 4: Text-Preserving Binarization & Despeckling\]                                           |  
|    ├── Sauvola local adaptive thresholding (k \= 0.20 to 0.35, window \= 25–45 px)                |  
|    └── Morphological area opening (removing isolated noise specks \< 3 px)                         |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

### **Document Boundary Localization and Perspective Rectification**

Incoming field photographs must first be segmented from their capture backgrounds, which often include scale counters, vehicle clipboards, or steering wheels. The image is downscaled to an operational resolution of 1080p and processed with a bilateral filter to suppress non-uniform surface textures while preserving sharp document boundary gradients:

![][image2]

Adaptive morphological gradient filtering paired with Canny edge detection isolates candidate boundary contours. The convex hull corresponding to the largest quadrangular polygon is identified. When four primary vertices ![][image3] are detected, a planar homography matrix ![][image4] is computed to map the quadrilateral into a canonical rectangular bounding box, eliminating perspective convergence3. If severe non-planar curling or surface folds dominate, the pipeline fits a thin-plate spline model across estimated text baselines to dewarp the curved substrate into an orthorectified plane3.

### **Orientation Correction and Baseline Deskewing**

Weighbridge tickets captured by mobile devices frequently arrive inverted (![][image5]) or rotated sideways (![][image6]). An initial four-class convolutional orientation classifier standardizes the receipt into an upright orientation.

Once oriented, fine rotational skew within a ![][image7] range must be eliminated to prevent downstream text line segmentation failures3. Text lines create concentrated directional frequency responses. Applying the Radon transform across candidate angles measures line projection integrals:

![][image8]

The angle ![][image9] that maximizes projection variance corresponds to the primary text orientation. Applying an inverse affine rotation matrix realigns text baselines parallel to the horizontal axis within an error margin of ![][image10], preventing fragmented word tokens during bounding-box construction3.

### **Illumination Normalization and Contrast Enhancement**

To counteract severe lighting gradients and restore faded thermal text, the rectified image is transformed into the CIE LAB color space, decoupling luminance (![][image11]) from chromaticity channels (![][image12]). A morphological background model is computed using a disk structuring element ![][image13] sized larger than the thickest character stroke, typically with a radius of ![][image14]:

![][image15]

Dividing the original image by this background model eliminates low-frequency illumination variations, shadows, and edge vignetting:

![][image16]

Following division normalization, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) is applied over contextual tiles of ![][image17] with a contrast clip limit of ![][image18]3. CLAHE redistributes local luminance densities, amplifying the edge gradients of faint thermal printing without amplifying broad-spectrum background noise3.

### **Dynamic Adaptive Binarization**

Global thresholding techniques, such as Otsu binarization, perform poorly on degraded thermal paper because they assume a bimodal histogram distribution across the entire frame3. When thermal media exhibits uneven background darkening or chemical fading, Otsu binarization systematically erases faint character strokes in pale sections while merging text and noise into solid black artifacts in darker regions3.

The architecture addresses this by implementing Sauvola local adaptive binarization, which adjusts the threshold ![][image19] based on local pixel statistics3:

![][image20]

In this formulation, ![][image21] and ![][image22] represent the local sample mean and standard deviation computed over a rectangular window of size ![][image23], calibrated to ![][image24] at 300 DPI3. The parameter ![][image25] denotes the dynamic range of standard deviation, fixed at ![][image26] for 8-bit grayscale, while ![][image27] is a control parameter calibrated between ![][image28] and ![][image29]3. In high-contrast regions with crisp text, ![][image22] is large, driving ![][image19] downward to track ink boundaries tightly. In low-contrast regions affected by fading, ![][image22] approaches zero, which lowers the threshold to capture weak character strokes without amplifying background paper texture3. Following binarization, morphological area opening eliminates isolated noise artifacts smaller than 3 pixels while preserving stroke connectivity3.

&nbsp;

| Preprocessing Stage | Target Physical Artifact | Mathematical / Algorithmic Operation | Downstream Recognition Impact |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Perspective Warp** | Oblique mobile angle, keystone distortion3 | 4-point homography transform via convex hull detection3 | Eliminates spatial scale drift; normalizes character aspect ratios3 |
| **Deskewing** | Angular misalignment (![][image7])3 | Radon transform projection profiling; affine rotation3 | Prevents cross-line bounding-box fragmentation3 |
| **Background Division** | Non-uniform shadows, cab chassis occlusion3 | Morphological opening background modeling (![][image30])3 | Removes non-linear illumination gradients3 |
| **CLAHE** | Faded leuco dye, low optical contrast3 | Contextual histogram equalization (clip limit ![][image18], tile ![][image31])3 | Amplifies faint stroke edges for text detection3 |
| **Sauvola Binarization** | Uneven discoloration, stains, pin voids3 | Local variance-guided adaptive thresholding (![][image32])3 | Preserves character topology without noise blooming3 |

## **Comparative Evaluation of Document Intelligence and OCR Engines**

Selecting an extraction engine for municipal weighbridge receipts requires balancing character recognition accuracy, spatial layout modeling, processing latency, operational cost, and data privacy across open-source and proprietary platforms1.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| OCR ARCHITECTURAL TRADE-OFF MATRIX                                                                |  
\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| Engine          | Paradigm             | Strengths                     | Critical Failure Modes   |  
\+-----------------+----------------------+-------------------------------+--------------------------+  
| Amazon Textract | Cloud Multimodal API | Native key-value / queries    | Closed-box, high latency |  
|                 |                      | Turnkey tabular parsing       | Degrades on faint print  |  
| PaddleOCR v4    | Modular Deep CV      | Extreme speed, low compute    | Requires layout parser   |  
|                 | (DBNet++ / SVTR)     | Robust on scene text & receipts| Uncalibrated confidences |  
| docTR           | Modular Deep CV      | Native PyTorch/ONNX support   | Slower on high-density   |  
|                 | (DBNet / SAR-CRNN)   | Clean programmatic control    | Lower baseline accuracy  |  
| LayoutLMv3      | Multimodal Layout    | SOTA spatial relation graph   | Requires pre-OCR input   |  
|                 | Transformer (Encoder)| Joint visual-textual parsing  | Heavy fine-tuning needed |  
| End-to-End VLMs | Autoregressive       | Unified end-to-end extraction | HIGH HALLUCINATION RISK  |  
| (Donut, GLM)    | Vision-to-Text VLM   | No OCR pipeline required      | Will invent missing digits|  
\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Amazon Textract provides managed document processing through its specialized AnalyzeDocument endpoints, using proprietary multi-task vision-language architectures4. Its FORMS and QUERIES features support schema extraction by processing natural language prompts alongside geometric document representations4. While Textract demonstrates high accuracy on standard commercial documentation, it experiences performance drops on severely faded thermal receipts unless paired with contrast-restoration preprocessing4. Furthermore, its dependency on cloud infrastructure introduces recurring per-page API costs and network latency, which can conflict with data sovereignty requirements in secure municipal environments6.

PaddleOCR, built on the PP-OCRv4 framework, represents an effective open-source alternative for receipt and scene text processing1. PP-OCRv4 pairs Differentiable Binarization (DBNet++) for text detection with a lightweight SVTR-LCNet backbone for text recognition1. Because it is designed to handle unconstrained scene text, PP-OCRv4 exhibits strong resilience against broken dot-matrix characters, thermal pin dropouts, and low-contrast stroke fragments1. Its lightweight runtime footprint (![][image33] total model parameters) allows it to run on edge hardware or local central processors with inference latencies under 50 milliseconds1. However, it outputs unstructured bounding boxes and text strings, requiring downstream geometric logic to associate key-value pairs2.

Other open-source options include docTR (Mindee) and LayoutLMv37. While docTR offers modular PyTorch and ONNX execution architectures, its standard recognition heads demonstrate lower baseline accuracy on degraded dot-matrix thermal fonts compared to PP-OCRv41. LayoutLMv3 provides multimodal layout modeling by jointly encoding text tokens, visual patches, and 2D spatial bounding boxes via self-attention mechanisms8. Although LayoutLMv3 excels at extracting entities from varied document structures, it functions strictly as a downstream parser that depends entirely on the accuracy of upstream OCR tokenizers8.

&nbsp;

| Engine / Framework | Core Architecture | Resilience to Thermal Degradation | Structured Extraction Capability | Latency & Resource Footprint | Deployment Model & Data Sovereignty |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Amazon Textract** (AnalyzeDocument) | Cloud Multimodal Vision-Language Backbone4 | Moderate; requires external contrast restoration on faded tickets4. | Exceptional; native FORMS and QUERIES parse key-value pairs without templates4. | Latency ![][image34]; managed cloud infrastructure6. | Proprietary cloud SaaS; per-page consumption fees; off-premise routing6. |
| **PaddleOCR** (PP-OCRv4 \+ PP-Structure) | DBNet++ detection and SVTR-LCNet character recognition1 | High; scene-text training handles broken dot-matrix printing1. | Modular; requires spatial token grouping or PP-Structure modules2. | Latency ![][image35] GPU, ![][image36] CPU; footprint ![][image33]6. | Apache 2.0 Open-Source; fully self-hosted; edge and local deployment6. |
| **docTR** (Mindee) | DBNet text detection paired with CRNN / SAR recognizers7 | Moderate; sensitive to character stroke disconnects1. | Basic; generates raw words and lines; requires custom spatial parsing7. | Latency ![][image37] GPU; standard PyTorch runtime7. | Apache 2.0 Open-Source; self-hosted; zero API cost. |
| **LayoutLMv3** (Microsoft) | Multimodal Transformer (text tokens, visual patches, 2D coordinates)8 | Dependent on upstream OCR engine tokenization quality8. | Exceptional; sequence labeling assigns semantic entity classes8. | Latency ![][image38] GPU; requires dedicated GPU acceleration8. | Open-weight research model; self-hosted; requires fine-tuning on domain data. |
| **End-to-End Generative VLMs** (Donut, GLM-OCR) | Autoregressive Encoder-Decoder Transformer; direct image-to-text generation2 | Highly volatile; attention drifts across low-contrast sections2. | High; generates structured JSON payloads directly from prompts2. | Latency ![][image39] GPU; footprint ![][image40] VRAM2. | Open-weight; high compute costs; introduces critical hallucination risks2. |

End-to-end generative vision-language models like Donut and Nougat process document images directly into structured text representations, bypassing explicit OCR detection and recognition steps2. While this approach simplifies the pipeline, it introduces a critical failure mode: unconstrained autoregressive hallucination2. When an autoregressive decoder encounters an illegible digit obscured by a grease stain or thermal fade, its internal language model priors force it to emit the most statistically probable continuation token2. In a municipal audit context, a model that generates a plausible tare weight such as 14,180 from an unreadable receipt introduces fabricated data into the public record2. Consequently, generative end-to-end decoders are unsuitable for evidentiary document processing. Municipal verification systems require an extractive architecture where every extracted character is tied to a verifiable bounding box, an image crop, and calibrated OCR probabilities4.

## **Layout-Aware Extraction and Spatial Parsing Architecture**

Weighbridge receipts follow varied vendor formats (e.g., Rice Lake, Fairbanks, Avery Weigh-Tronix, Mettler Toledo), but their visual structures generally map to two main layout topologies: key-value anchored pairs and columnar tables1.

|  TICKET NO : 0098421           DATE: 2024-05-12        TICKET: 0098421               TRUCK: H-9921|

\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

To extract target fields without relying on fragile fixed pixel coordinates, the system constructs a spatial token graph over all detected text elements2. The OCR engine returns a discrete token set ![][image41], where each token ![][image42] contains a recognized string value ![][image43], bounding box coordinates ![][image44], and confidence score ![][image45]6.

A directed adjacency graph ![][image46] is established over these tokens using spatial geometric rules2:

* **Horizontal Key-Value Association**: Directed edges link label tokens to adjacent values if their vertical overlap exceeds 60% (![][image47]), the value token is situated to the right (![][image48]), and the horizontal gap is within 3.5 times the mean character width.  
* **Vertical Columnar Association**: In tabular scale tickets, directed vertical edges connect column headers downwards if horizontal overlap exceeds 50%, the value token is positioned below (![][image49]), and the vertical pitch is within 2.0 times the line height.

Entity extraction begins by locating semantic anchors using normalized alias lexicons:

* Gross Weight Aliases: gross, gross wt, gr wt, brutto, g.w.  
* Tare Weight Aliases: tare, tare wt, tr wt, t.w.  
* Net Weight Aliases: net, net wt, n.w., netto  
* Ticket Identifier Aliases: ticket, ticket no, tk no, rec no, scale ticket, inv no  
* Vehicle Identifier Aliases: truck, truck no, vehicle, veh no, plate, reg no  
* Weighbridge Scale Aliases: scale, scale id, weighbridge, station, terminal

Because thermal print degradation often causes character recognition errors in anchor text (such as GROSS being misread as CR0SS or GR0SS), tokens are matched against the alias lexicons using normalized Levenshtein distance1:

![][image50]

Tokens with similarity scores of ![][image51] are marked as candidate anchor nodes. The system then traverses outgoing graph edges to identify associated values, validating candidates against target regular expressions (such as numeric weight formats ^\\d{1,3}(,\\d{3})\*(\\.\\d{1,2})?$) to confirm extraction accuracy.

## **Forensic Validation and Arithmetic Reconciliation Engine**

Extracted OCR text represents unverified visual data. To establish legally defensible records for municipal audits, extractions must pass through an automated validation engine that enforces mathematical, structural, and operational invariants2.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| DETERMINISTIC ARITHMETIC AND RELATIONAL RECONCILIATION GATE                                      |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                                                                                                  |  
|    \[Extracted Gross Weight: G\]   \[Extracted Tare Weight: T\]    \[Extracted Net Weight: N\]         |  
|                 \\                         |                         /                            |  
|                  \\                        |                        /                             |  
|                   v                       v                       v                              |  
|              \+---------------------------------------------------------+                         |  
|              | ARITHMETIC RECONCILIATION INVARIANT                     |                         |  
|              |                                                         |                         |  
|              |     Reconciliation Delta:  Δ \= |(G \- T) \- N|             |                         |  
|              |                                                         |                         |  
|              |     Condition 1: Δ \== 0  (Exact Zero Tolerance)         |                         |  
|              |     Condition 2: G \> T \> 0                              |                         |  
|              |     Condition 3: T\_min \<= T \<= T\_max (Vehicle Envelope) |                         |  
|              \+---------------------------------------------------------+                         |  
|                                           |                                                      |  
|                   \+-----------------------+-----------------------+                              |  
|                   |                                               |                              |  
|                   v                                               v                              |  
|         \[Reconciliation Pass\]                           \[Reconciliation Fail\]                    |  
|                   |                                               |                              |  
|     Verified Evidentiary Baseline                   Trigger Deterministic Digit Repair           |  
|     (Eligible for Straight-Through)                 or Escalate to Human Auditor UI              |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

### **The Arithmetic Invariant**

Weighbridge tickets record a closed physical mass balance: a vehicle enters the facility, its total load is measured (Gross), its unladen weight is determined (Tare), and the difference represents the delivered material (Net)2. This transaction adheres to a strict arithmetic constraint2:

![][image52]

The validation engine evaluates the absolute reconciliation discrepancy:

![][image53]

Because modern commercial vehicle scales operate with discrete measurement increments (typically ![][image54] or ![][image55]), the allowable margin for arithmetic error is zero:

![][image56]

Any discrepancy greater than zero indicates an optical character substitution error, physical scale malfunction, or document manipulation9.

### **Domain Boundary and Physical Envelope Invariants**

Extracted weight values must also fall within physical transportation bounds:

* Monotonic Ordering: ![][image57] and ![][image58].  
* Gross Vehicle Weight Rating Limits: In municipal civil works, commercial haulage vehicles adhere to statutory axle weight regulations. A standard three-axle dump truck has an unladen tare weight between ![][image59] and ![][image60] and a gross operational ceiling near ![][image61]. A tractor-trailer combination operates up to ![][image62] (or statutory regional equivalents, such as ![][image63]). Extracted tare weights falling outside these envelopes (e.g., an unladen weight of ![][image64] for a tandem-axle vehicle) point to dropped leading digits during character recognition (12,180 misread as 2,180).  
* Minimum Net Mass Threshold: A calculated net payload below ![][image65] for bulk aggregate hauling flags a potential misaligned field association or incomplete loading cycle.

### **Syntactic Normalization and Registry Cross-Referencing**

Extracted strings are normalized into structured data types:

* Vehicle Registration Formatting: Extracted plate strings are stripped of whitespace and punctuation, converted to uppercase, and matched against jurisdictional registration syntax. The sanitized identifier is cross-referenced against the municipal contract’s authorized fleet database; unrecognized plates are flagged for unapproved equipment usage.  
* Temporal Consistency: Dates and times are converted to ISO-8601 UTC strings (![][image66]) and validated against contract operational windows (![][image67]). Tickets dated outside authorized working windows or after invoice submission dates generate audit warnings.  
* Weighbridge Identification: The scale terminal identifier is cross-checked against municipal or state registries of certified commercial measurement devices to verify calibration currency.

## **Uncertainty Quantification, Confidence Calibration, and Strict Abstention**

To maintain audit integrity, the platform combines multiple confidence signals and enforces an explicit abstention policy, preventing the ingestion of unverified values2.

### **Multi-Factor Confidence Formulation**

Relying solely on raw OCR Softmax probabilities can be misleading, as deep neural networks frequently assign high confidence to misread characters when processing out-of-distribution thermal fonts9. The platform calculates field confidence using a multi-factor scoring model that incorporates character probabilities, spatial alignment, and syntax compliance6:

![][image68]

Here, the first term represents the geometric mean of individual character recognition probabilities ![][image69] across the ![][image70] tokens forming the field6. The spatial component ![][image71] penalizes candidate values based on their distance from the anchor label and angular deviation from the text baseline:

![][image72]

The syntactic component ![][image73] applies a binary or scaled penalty (![][image74] vs. ![][image75]) based on regular expression compliance. The exponents are balanced to prioritize optical and structural quality (![][image76]).

The overall Document Confidence Score combines field-level scores with arithmetic verification:

![][image77]

where ![][image78] and ![][image79] is an indicator function returning ![][image80] if arithmetic reconciliation succeeds (![][image81]) and ![][image82] if it fails. If arithmetic reconciliation fails, the overall document confidence drops to zero, preventing automated ingestion.

\+--------------------------------------------------------------+---------------+--------------------+

### **Deterministic Digit Repair Hypotheses**

When arithmetic validation fails (![][image83]) due to an isolated OCR misread on a degraded receipt, the system avoids open-ended model generation. Instead, it tests for known character confusion patterns caused by thermal printhead pin dropouts1:

![][image84]

If two weight fields exhibit high confidence (![][image85]) while the third contains low-confidence tokens (![][image86]), the missing or corrupted value is computed algebraically2:

![][image87]

If this algebraically derived value matches the low-confidence string with exactly one character substitution belonging to ![][image88], the system generates a **Deterministic Repair Hypothesis**1. This hypothesis is never committed to the database automatically; it is presented to human reviewers as an annotated suggestion within the verification interface, maintaining a verifiable audit trail.

| Operational Triage Lane | Decision Criteria | System Routing Action | Evidentiary Audit Status |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Lane 1: Straight-Through** | **![][image89]**, ![][image81], registry valid | Automated ingestion into payment ledger | Legally certified; touchless execution |
| **Lane 2: Human Review** | **![][image90]**, ![][image81], or fleet mismatch | Escalate to verification UI with bounding-box focus | Pending auditor sign-off |
| **Lane 3: Hard Abstention** | **![][image91]**, ![][image83], or critical field missing | Terminate extraction; issue rescan request | Rejected; non-evidentiary record |

### **Local Open-Source Architecture (BUILD IT)**

The local pipeline is structured for environments requiring complete data isolation, zero external API costs, and deterministic execution on on-premise hardware1:

* **Ingestion Endpoint**: A FastAPI asynchronous service receives multi-part image uploads, calculates SHA-256 integrity hashes, and creates tracking records in a local PostgreSQL database.  
* **Worker Queue**: Tasks are dispatched across a Redis message broker to Celery worker nodes.  
* **Image Restoration Service**: OpenCV workers execute Canny contour detection, perspective homography rectification, orientation correction, morphological background division, and Sauvola adaptive binarization3.  
* **OCR Inference**: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 processes the restored imagery, extracting text tokens, spatial coordinates, and confidence values1.  
* **Spatial Parsing**: A geometric graph module connects tokens using horizontal and vertical projection bounds, mapping candidate values to identified semantic anchors2.  
* **Validation Core**: A Pydantic v2 validation service evaluates regular expressions, enforces the arithmetic invariant (![][image92]), checks vehicle fleet registries, and computes composite confidence scores2.  
* **Persistence & Review**: High-confidence extractions commit directly to PostgreSQL; exceptions route to a Streamlit review console for manual verification.

### **Cloud-Native AWS Architecture (SHIP IT)**

The cloud configuration uses managed serverless infrastructure to support automated scaling, high availability, and compliance auditing4:

* **Ingestion Tier**: Clients authenticate via Amazon API Gateway to obtain pre-signed Amazon S3 URLs, uploading images directly to an ingestion bucket (s3://muniaudit-raw/).  
* **Orchestration Engine**: An S3 event notification triggers an AWS Step Functions state machine that coordinates downstream Lambda execution and handles failure retries.  
* **Preprocessing Lambda**: An AWS Lambda container running OpenCV and Leptonica performs perspective correction, CLAHE contrast recovery, and deskewing, outputting clean images to an intermediate bucket3.  
* **Textract Extraction**: Step Functions invokes Amazon Textract AnalyzeDocument using both FORMS and QUERIES modes4. Natural language queries extract target values directly:  
  * What is the ticket number?  
  * What is the truck or vehicle number?  
  * What is the gross weight?  
  * What is the tare weight?  
  * What is the net weight?  
  * What is the date?  
  * What is the time?  
  * What is the weighbridge scale ID?  
* **Validation Lambda**: A downstream Lambda parses Textract responses, normalizes numeric values, evaluates the arithmetic equation, and assigns triage classifications2.  
* **Human Review Routing**: Extractions flagged with low confidence or arithmetic discrepancies route directly to Amazon Augmented AI (A2I), generating human review tasks in a private workforce console6.  
* **Persistence**: Approved records are written to Amazon DynamoDB, while raw images, Textract JSON payloads, and audit trails are archived in Amazon S3 Glacier.

&nbsp;

| Pipeline Function | Local / Open-Source Implementation (BUILD IT) | Cloud-Native AWS Architecture (SHIP IT) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **API / Ingestion** | FastAPI running inside Docker; Redis message broker | Amazon API Gateway with Pre-Signed Amazon S3 URLs |
| **Preprocessing** | OpenCV Python/C++ (CLAHE, Deskew, Sauvola)3 | AWS Lambda (OCI Container image with OpenCV/Leptonica)3 |
| **OCR Core** | PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 via ONNX Runtime / TensorRT6 | Amazon Textract (AnalyzeDocument with QUERIES API)4 |
| **Layout Parsing** | Spatial token adjacency graph & fuzzy anchor search2 | Native Textract Key-Value Forms & Natural Language Queries6 |
| **Validation Engine** | Pydantic v2 core enforcing arithmetic checks2 | AWS Lambda microservice querying DynamoDB/ElastiCache caches2 |
| **Human Review** | Streamlit web console displaying interactive bounding boxes | Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) human review workflows6 |
| **Data Ledger** | PostgreSQL database with structured JSONB audit storage | Amazon DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery & S3 Glacier archival |

## **Human-in-the-Loop Workflow and Exception Resolution UI**

The review interface is structured to facilitate rapid manual verification while preventing confirmation bias during data entry2. When an extraction is flagged for review, the auditor is presented with the original image alongside the extracted data fields, with low-confidence areas visually highlighted.

Selecting an input field automatically pans and magnifies the corresponding bounding box on the original document image. Reviewers can adjust contrast sliders or toggle between raw RGB and binarized views to inspect faint thermal text. A live calculation bar validates the arithmetic balance (![][image93]) in real time as values are adjusted, blocking submission until the invariant is satisfied. Any manual modifications are logged with reviewer metadata, timestamps, and justification codes to preserve evidentiary audit trails.

## **End-to-End Operational Pipeline and Evidence Dossier Schema**

The verification pipeline executes as an integrated process across eight operational stages:

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| COMPLETE PIPELINE EXECUTION TRACE                                                                |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
| 1\. Upload & Ingestion       Multi-part upload with cryptographic SHA-256 payload generation      |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 2\. Image Preprocessing      Perspective rectification, deskewing, background division, CLAHE,    |  
|                             and Sauvola adaptive binarization                                    |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 3\. OCR Feature Extraction   PaddleOCR / Amazon Textract returns tokens, geometry, probabilities  |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 4\. Layout-Aware Parsing     Spatial token graph traversal maps values to semantic anchor labels  |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 5\. Value Normalization      Sanitizes weight strings to floats, standardizes dates to ISO-8601,  |  
|                             formats vehicle license plate alphanumeric patterns                  |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 6\. Forensic Validation      Enforces Gross \- Tare \= Net, verifies vehicle envelope limits, checks|  
|                             fleet registration status, validates weighbridge registry records   |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 7\. Uncertainty Assessment   Calculates composite field confidence; evaluates against thresholds  |  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 8\. Triage & Routing         Direct commit (Lane 1), human review (Lane 2), hard rejection (Lane 3)|  
|                                                                                                  |  
| 9\. Audit Dossier Output     Persists structured JSON record, bounding box coordinates, and logs  |  
\+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Incoming image streams are hashed and preprocessed to correct perspective, skew, and contrast variations3. The OCR engine extracts text tokens, spatial bounding boxes, and confidence scores, which are organized into structured fields by the spatial parsing layer2. Normalization modules standardize values into canonical data formats before the forensic engine evaluates arithmetic balance, vehicle parameters, and registry records2. Finally, the uncertainty framework calculates composite confidence scores, routing the result to straight-through processing, manual review, or hard rejection2.

## **Phased Implementation Roadmap and Hackathon MVP Recommendation**

To deliver a functional proof-of-concept within a rapid hackathon timeframe while planning for enterprise adoption, system capabilities are structured across two implementation tiers1:

&nbsp;

| Subsystem Component | Hackathon MVP Scope | Enterprise Production Scope | Technical Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Image Preprocessing** | OpenCV Python: Deskewing via Radon/Hough \+ CLAHE \+ Sauvola binarization3. | Containerized C++ OpenCV/Leptonica: Thin-plate spline dewarping \+ neural edge extraction3. | Python OpenCV handles 85% of thermal contrast and orientation issues on standard CPU hardware3. |
| **OCR Recognition** | Local PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 CPU inference1. | AWS Textract AnalyzeDocument with QUERIES API4. | PaddleOCR provides fast, open-source OCR without requiring cloud provisioning or incurring API fees1. |
| **Information Extraction** | Spatial token grouping using bounding-box heuristics and regex matching2. | Hybrid: Textract Queries with LayoutLMv3 fallback for non-standard formats6. | Geometric anchor search parses structured receipts with minimal configuration2. |
| **Forensic Validation** | Deterministic arithmetic check (![][image94]) \+ regex license plate formatting2. | Direct integration with municipal fleet lists and certified weighbridge scale databases2. | Arithmetic verification detects OCR misreads and potential ticket manipulation out of the box. |
| **Human Review UI** | Streamlit web console featuring interactive bounding boxes and form editing. | Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) integrated into enterprise municipal ERP portals6. | Streamlit provides rapid UI development for proof-of-concept validation workflows. |
| **Data Storage** | Local SQLite / PostgreSQL with structured JSON schemas. | Amazon DynamoDB with S3 Glacier archival and object-lock compliance policies. | Relational databases support rapid local schema iteration without cloud dependencies. |

The hackathon MVP prioritizes the core extraction and validation loop: an OpenCV preprocessing pipeline (featuring CLAHE and Sauvola binarization), a local PaddleOCR recognition engine, and an automated Pydantic validation script enforcing the arithmetic invariant (![][image94])1. A Streamlit web dashboard provides an interactive interface to showcase receipt processing, highlight low-confidence extractions, demonstrate pin-dropout repair hypotheses, and verify mathematical integrity before saving to the database.

For enterprise production, the architecture migrates to the managed AWS serverless topology. This transition incorporates the Amazon Textract Queries API, connects to Amazon A2I for workforce exception handling, integrates live municipal vehicle registration databases, and establishes immutable audit logs within Amazon DynamoDB4.

## **Architectural Conclusions and Strategic Synthesis**

Implementing an automated document-intelligence system for thermal weighbridge receipts requires addressing physical media decay, optical noise, and strict evidentiary audit standards1. Standard commercial OCR engines and generative multimodal vision-language models encounter significant hurdles in this domain: cloud APIs frequently degrade on faint thermal printing without targeted preprocessing, while generative VLMs introduce risks of silent character hallucinations when processing obscured text2.

The proposed architecture resolves these challenges through a modular processing design:

* Optical Recovery: The front-end pipeline combines background division, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), and Sauvola adaptive binarization to lift faint thermal text from discolored paper, neutralizing non-uniform shadows and contrast loss before OCR execution3.  
* Extractive Information Parsing: Enforcing an extractive-only architecture using localized bounding boxes and spatial adjacency graphs grounds all extracted values directly in visible document imagery, eliminating hallucination risks2.  
* Deterministic Forensic Gates: Extracted values must satisfy the fundamental arithmetic invariant (![][image94]), conform to statutory vehicle weight limits, and match municipal fleet registries before approval2.  
* Calibrated Abstention Protocols: When character confidence falls below established thresholds or arithmetic checks fail, the system refrains from guessing. It flags exceptions for human review via an interactive interface that displays localized bounding boxes and candidate repair hypotheses2.

By deploying this layered architecture—whether through an open-source PaddleOCR stack or a managed AWS Textract pipeline—municipal oversight bodies can streamline invoice processing while maintaining mathematical accuracy, evidentiary integrity, and protection against fraudulent billing1.
